articles.title: Caroline Dubois fights Stephanie Han in three-belt world championship unification on February 20 live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Stephanie Han in Texas on February 20 live on Sky Sports in UK prime time; Dubois and Han will fight to unify the WBC, WBO and WBA lightweight world titles; "I'm coming to take her title and show everyone why I'm the best lightweight in the world," Dubois said
articles.body:
The unbeaten champions will fight at GECU Arena at the Don Haskins Center in El Paso with three world titles on the line as London's Dubois travels to fight Han in front of her hometown fans.

Most Valuable Promotion's unified WBC and WBO lightweight world champion, Dubois is one of the most accomplished young talents in women's boxing.

"I can't wait to get back in the ring and I can't wait to go into Stephanie Han's hometown and add another world title to my collection," Dubois said.

"I respect what she's accomplished, but I'm coming to El Paso to take her title and show everyone why I'm the best lightweight in the world.

"These are the kinds of fights I've been working toward my entire career. I want all the belts, I want the biggest fights, and I want to prove myself against the best. On Saturday, February 20, I'm coming to make a statement and take another step toward becoming undisputed.

"A big thank you to MVP and Sky for making this fight happen and continuing to give women's boxing the platform it deserves."

The southpaw known as "Sweet Caroline" enjoyed a decorated amateur career that included gold at the 2018 Youth Olympic Games, four European Youth Championships and representing Great Britain at the Tokyo Olympics.

Turning professional in 2022, Dubois quickly established herself as a dominant force in the lightweight division, capturing the WBC world title before unifying the WBC and WBO championships with a victory over Terri Harper at MVPW-01 in April.

She most recently defended her titles against Amelia Moore in August and now looks to add the WBA championship to her collection in the biggest unification fight of her professional career.

Han is an El Paso native, a devoted mother of two, veteran of the El Paso Police Department and former beauty pageant competitor whose remarkable journey has made her one of the most compelling figures in women's boxing.

Known as "The Enforcer," Han captured the vacant WBA lightweight world title with a first-round knockout of Hannah Terlep in 2025 and has since successfully defended her championship three times, including back-to-back victories over combat sports legend Holly Holm.

Most recently Han defeated Holm in front of her hometown fans in El Paso in May, further cementing her status as one of the division's elite champions.

She will now face the biggest challenge of her career at GECU Arena at the Don Haskins Center, with an opportunity to unify three major world titles.

Han said: "This fight is a dream come true! Finally, I have the opportunity to unify titles in my division and get one step closer to becoming the undisputed queen of the lightweight division.

"To be able to fight at home at GECU Arena at the Don Haskins Center is incredibly special, and I'm grateful to MVP for their support to make this happen. I invite all of El Paso to come out and support on Saturday, February 20 and witness this moment."

Nakisa Bidarian, CEO of Most Valuable Promotions, said: "Caroline Dubois and Stephanie Han are two undefeated world champions at the top of one of the deepest and most competitive divisions in boxing.

"Stephanie's story is remarkable. She's a police officer, a mother, a former beauty queen and a world champion who has become a source of pride for El Paso.

"Caroline has established herself as one of the most talented young champions in the sport, and bringing these two women together with three major world titles on the line is a huge moment for MVP and women's boxing.

"El Paso has shown up for its hometown hero time and time again, so we owed it to this city to bring one of the biggest fights in boxing to GECU Arena at the Don Haskins Center on Saturday, February 20, live in UK prime time on Sky Sports."

articles.title: Ilia Topuria pone fecha a su regreso: "A partir de abril..."
articles.standfirst: Dana White, 'boss' de la UFC, había hablado de principios de 2027
articles.summary: Dana White, 'boss' de la UFC, había hablado de principios de 2027
articles.body: El retorno de Ilia Topuria (17-1) al octágono de la UFC no se producirá antes de abril. Una fecha que ya habíamos dejado caer en MARCA pero que ahora el 'Matador' ha confirmado públicamente en una entrevista con Álvaro Colmenero en 'ABC'. El doble campeón hispanogeorgiano, por lo tanto, niega la opción que declaró Dana White', presidente de UFC, de que estuviera peleando "a principios de 2027". "A partir de abril es cuando estamos considerando la vuelta", declaraba Topuria. El ex campeón del peso ligero, despojado de su corona por Justin Gaethje el pasado 14 de junio, lleva más de un mes en Georgia con su familia, completando su recuperación y volviendo a los entrenamientos. Topuria, mientras, ha calentado su 'retorno' lanzando una encuesta en Instagram y preguntando a sus seguidores cuál debería ser su próximo rival: Justin Gaethje, buscando una revancha por el título... o Paddy Pimblett. "Paddy, Paddy, Paddy. Me lo comeré como la salchicha que es", decía en 'ABC'. En ningún caso menciona a Arman Tsarukyan, #2 de la división y, para muchos, gran aspirante al título. Topuria, mientras, promete volver a lo grande: "En el próximo combate veréis una versión mía que no habías visto nunca". Son unas palabras que acompaña de la confirmación de que no ha perdido "el fuego interior"... y de que sumar una derrota no ha cambiado nada en su hambre de seguir haciendo historia. Tras ser doble campeón de la UFC, el primero en lograrlo invicto, ya piensa en su próximo paso: y este está en la división del peso ligero. Volver al peso pluma no parece una opción.

articles.title: Dubois vs Han: Britain's Caroline Dubois will fight American Stephanie Han in lightweight unification bout
articles.summary: Britain's Caroline Dubois will take on American Stephanie Han in a lightweight unification bout on 20 February in Texas.
articles.body:
Britain's Caroline Dubois will take on American Stephanie Han in a lightweight unification bout on 20 February in America.

Dubois, 25, is the reigning WBC and WBO champion and will travel to the Gecu Arena at the Don Haskins Center in El Paso, Texas, to take on WBA title holder Han.

Londoner Dubois, who is undefeated as a professional with 14 wins and one draw, unified her titles in April 2026 with a decision win against Terri Harper.

Han, 36, is also undefeated with 13 wins and has defended her WBA belt three times, including two victories over former UFC champion Holly Holm in 2026.

"I can't wait to get back in the ring and I can't wait to go into Stephanie Han's hometown and add another world title to my collection," said Dubois.

"I respect what she's accomplished, but I'm coming to El Paso to take her title.

"These are the kinds of fights I've been working toward my entire career. I want all the belts, I want the biggest fights, and I want to prove myself against the best."

Hutchinson's mission to fulfil childhood prophecy

From street fighter to world champion - Bentley's rise to top

The fourth belt in the exciting lightweight division will be put on the line on Sunday when undefeated IBF champion Elif Nur Turhan takes on American Alycia Baumgardner in Texas.

Dubois and Baumgardner have made no secret of their desire to fight each other and if both were to come through their respective bouts with victories they could meet in an undisputed contest in 2027.

Both fighters are signed to Most Valuable Promotions, making the possibility of them meeting highly likely.

Dubois is aiming to become just the fifth Briton to earn undisputed status in the four-belt era after Josh Taylor, Chantelle Cameron, Savannah Marshall and Ellie Scotney.

Seven years Dubois' senior, Baumgardner is regarded as one of the best pound-for-pound boxers, but the Briton was not shy in confronting her rival in the post-fight interview of her August win against Amelia Moore.

Dubois confirmed on social media that she will be ringside to watch Turkey's Turhan and Baumgardner, who is stepping up from super-featherweight.

articles.title: Connal McDonald's warning for Lucas Roehrig: 'I beat Daniel Dubois in the amateurs. I'll be treating this the same'
articles.summary: Scottish champion Connal McDonald fights top cruiserweight prospect Lucas Roehrig this Saturday at the Copper Box Arena; The Zuffa Boxing 12 event is headlined by Chris Billam-Smith's clash with Cheavon Clarke, watch live on Sky Sports on Saturday
articles.body:
Roehrig is an exciting cruiserweight prospect, being expertly guided towards the top by former world champion George Groves.

But McDonald has underrated credentials. He is the Scottish titlist and was an experienced amateur. Notably in the unpaid ranks he beat Daniel Dubois in the final of the Great British Youth championships in 2014 when they were teenagers.

Dubois, of course, is now a formidable two-time heavyweight champion of the world.

"There was all this talk about his power, even at that age," McDonald told Sky Sports . "The win looks great now! But at the time I was very, very confident, borderline cocky."

He recalled: "I was a very different fighter when I was that age. When Daniel walked out he was massive, built like a superhero. I was 17 and he was either 16 or 17. I had the whole mindset of 'I'm going to smash him'.

"I was standing in that ring thinking: 'I'm going to school this guy, I'm going to smash him.'

"It was a tough fight. The one thing I can remember is he was easy to land on. I was landing quite a lot of shots. I definitely thought at the end of the fight, I definitely won but it was one of those things where looking back on it, it was a tough fight.

"But I never would have thought he would have went on to be [one of the world's best heavyweights]. You're talking Usyk and probably Daniel Dubois now. Just respect to him for what he's done."

McDonald warned Roehrig: "I've come a long way from then, I'm a different boxer but come fight night I'll be treating it the exact same.

"No matter who's in there I'm going to go in and win.

Watch Roehrig vs McDonald this Saturday live on Sky Sports .
